TF-00.shape: page header: title + standfirst beside it
TF-00.anatomy: H1 in columns 1–7 at 56/84 weight 300; one lead paragraph in columns 10–13 at 18/27 weight 300. No image, no CTA. 48px top pad, 120px bottom.
TF-00.good_for: An inner-page opening where the answer can sit to the right of the title instead of under it.

TF-01.shape: full-bleed still with a credit/caption strip
TF-01.anatomy: One 16:9 still across the full 1264 content width, then a strip below: long caption sentence left (cols 1–10), source credit + one circle-arrow link right.
TF-01.good_for: A single proof image with one sentence of context and one link — not a hero.

TF-02.shape: dark claim band with three titled rows in the right column
TF-02.anatomy: Near-black band. Claim headline left in columns 1–8 at 48/72/300. Three rows stacked in columns 10–16, each a 20px title over a 18/27 body, separated by 1px rules at 16% white.
TF-02.good_for: Three short supporting arguments that read *beside* a claim, not under it. The strongest Blackstone signature band.

TF-03.anatomy: Eyebrow + H2 top-left. Four full-width rows starting at column 5: 24px title, chevron right, hairline between. Row body opens on click.
TF-03.good_for: A directory of four audiences / four answers where the titles alone carry the scan.

TF-04.anatomy: A single full-bleed still (or video) with no heading and no copy above or below.
TF-04.good_for: A breather between two arguments; pacing, not information.

TF-05.shape: 3-up titled prose columns, no card chrome
TF-05.anatomy: Eyebrow with a 56px rule, then three columns of 20px title over 16/24 body, no fills, no borders, left-aligned; a second row of two items sits offset below.
TF-05.good_for: Three to six short principles or categories that need no images.

TF-06.shape: large still with a caption strip
TF-06.anatomy: One large still occupying the content width with an overlay circle-arrow, then a caption strip with a long left sentence and a right-hand credit.
TF-06.good_for: Evidence or a place photo with a single deep link.

PE-00.shape: page header: title + standfirst (same as TF-00)
PE-00.anatomy: H1 columns 1–4 at 56/84/300, lead columns 10–16 at 18/27/300. Wide empty middle.
PE-00.good_for: Inner-page opening with a short lead — the emptier variant.

PE-01.anatomy: One 16:9 still across the content width, no copy.

PE-02.shape: stat row: label left, two figures right
PE-02.anatomy: A section label in columns 1–3, then two cells in columns 9–16: small-caps label above, 1px rule under it, then the value. Values sit below the fold of the crop at 220px+.
PE-02.good_for: Two or three hard numbers with a section label — the 'at a glance' shape.

PE-03.shape: dark claim band with one supporting paragraph
PE-03.anatomy: Near-black band. Claim left in columns 1–8 at 48/72/300. Right column 10–16: bold 18px sub-head, then body.
PE-03.good_for: A single claim plus one dense paragraph of support.

PE-04.anatomy: H2 spanning the left half, then three cards: 16:9 still (352×198), 20px title, 16/24 body, circle-arrow link at the foot.
PE-04.good_for: Three portfolio cases / three products with imagery and one link each.

PE-05.anatomy: Three rows: 24px title + chevron, hairline between.
PE-05.good_for: Three-item version of the row directory.

PE-06.anatomy: Eyebrow + H2, then three cards: 16:9 still with a play badge, 18px title, 16/24 body, muted source line.

APM-00.shape: page header with one download action
APM-00.anatomy: H1 at the left edge, a two-line standfirst in the right column, and a single 'Download Brochure' link with a circle-arrow under it. 19 words in the whole band.
APM-00.good_for: A title band on an editorial page where the one useful action is a download, not a form.

APM-01.shape: three numbered columns under a claim
APM-01.anatomy: Eyebrow + H2, then three columns across the 16 tracks: a 96px numeral (01 / 02 / 03), a 20px title, and a 16/24 paragraph. No cards, no rules between them.
APM-01.good_for: Three steps, three reasons, or three audience types — the numeral does the sequencing so the copy does not have to.

APM-02.anatomy: Near-black band. H2 + one line, then a feature matrix: rows of capabilities down the left, product/route columns across, ticks and dashes in each cell with one column highlighted, plus a footnote in small type.
APM-02.good_for: Showing where several routes differ on the same axes. Only works when every cell can honestly be tick, dash or a short word.

APM-03.anatomy: H3 and a paragraph in columns 1–6; a labelled chart exhibit in columns 9–16 with its own caption line.
APM-03.good_for: One claim that a single chart proves. Never put two charts side by side here.

APM-04.shape: no-heading continuation: data table left, prose right
APM-04.anatomy: No H2 at all. A small data table in columns 1–7, a two-paragraph column in columns 10–16, and a footnote beneath in 12px.
APM-04.good_for: Continuing an argument from the band above. Use sparingly — a heading-less band hides its structure from scanning and from AI answers.

APM-05.shape: dark band: chart left, paragraph right
APM-05.anatomy: Near-black band. H3 + one lead line, a big chart exhibit in columns 1–9 with captions under the bars, a paragraph column in columns 11–16.
APM-05.good_for: A trend that needs one number read off a chart. Dark keeps the chart from looking like a dashboard widget.

APM-06.shape: claim + prose over a tick/cross matrix
APM-06.anatomy: H3, a paragraph, then a second paragraph, then a matrix whose cells hold circle-check icons, with column labels above and row labels down the side, and a note beneath.
APM-06.good_for: Comparing a handful of options on several dimensions without writing a table of sentences.

APM-07.anatomy: H2 'Read the complete …' at the left, two brochure covers as stills on the right, and one 'Download Brochure' circle-arrow link.
APM-07.good_for: One downloadable asset with a preview of what it is.

APM-08.anatomy: H3 'Frequently Asked Questions', then hairline rows: question at 16px with a chevron at the right, closed by default.
APM-08.good_for: FAQ. The only place an accordion is honest on this site, because the answer is a detail, not the argument.

APM-09.anatomy: Near-black band. H3 'Explore Essentials' + seven full-width rows on hairlines, each a label with a 44px outline circle-chevron at the right edge.
APM-09.good_for: A menu of deeper pages when there are more than four of them.

IR-00.shape: investor overview: H1 + lead + 3 figures + modules
IR-00.anatomy: H1 + one lead paragraph, then three figures in a row (label above, 40px value, muted caption), then H4 modules (Latest Financials, Shareholder Relations two-column).
IR-00.good_for: A stats-led summary page. Note: the rest of this microsite's modules are JavaScript-populated, so only this block was measurable.

BMX-00.good_for: A title band on a sparse page.

BMX-01.anatomy: 16:9 still across the content width, then 28px claim in columns 5–8 and 16/24 paragraph in columns 9–16.
BMX-01.good_for: A claim that needs one paragraph of support under a single still.

BMX-02.anatomy: Near-black band. 24px claim in columns 3–5, paragraph in columns 8–14, then a small-caps label + 56px figure bottom-left.
BMX-02.good_for: A claim, its support, and one number — all in one dark band.

BMX-03.anatomy: Dark 1/3 column: 20px title, one 16/24 line, then a small-caps label over a 56px figure.
BMX-03.good_for: A three-up of claim + metric. Only works when each item really has a number.

BMX-07.anatomy: Copy continues from the band above with no new heading.

BMX-08.anatomy: One line of copy + one still + link.

BMX-09.anatomy: Rows spanning columns 3–14: 24px label, 44px outline circle-plus right, hairline between.
BMX-09.good_for: A short directory where each row opens a longer answer.

BMX-10.anatomy: Title in columns 1–4, rows in columns 6–16: label + chevron, hairline between.
BMX-10.good_for: Legal or long-tail content that must stay findable but quiet.

HOME-00.shape: hero: display line left, small type right
HOME-00.anatomy: Near-black band. Two-line display H1 at the left edge, one 16px paragraph top-right in columns 12–16, no CTA, no image.
HOME-00.good_for: A statement opening — the emptiest, most confident hero in the library.

HOME-01.shape: promo carousel: still with floating card
HOME-01.anatomy: Near-black band. 16:9 still with a white card floating over it, then title left / paragraph right beneath, dot pagination + prev/next circles.
HOME-01.good_for: A featured story that rotates; heavy, use once per page at most.

HOME-02.anatomy: Centred eyebrow with the 48px rule above, centred claim at 48/72/300, then two columns: small label + 16/24 paragraph left; 56px figure + 12px muted caption right; circle-arrow Learn more under the paragraph.
HOME-02.good_for: The strongest 'claim + one number' band: centred claim, asymmetric support.

HOME-03.anatomy: Heading stack left in columns 1–5, a bordered panel of rows right in columns 9–15.
HOME-03.good_for: A claim with three short linked answers.

HOME-04.anatomy: One giant display line clipped at both edges.

HOME-06.anatomy: H2 + four cards in a row with 16:9 stills and 16px titles.

HOME-07.shape: email capture: heading left, form right
HOME-07.anatomy: Near-black band. H2 + line left in columns 1–6, 6-field form right in columns 9–14.
HOME-07.good_for: A capture form. Not for a funding page.

FAL-00.shape: Falcon hero: display H1 + aside + full-bleed still + caption bar
FAL-00.anatomy: Darker band. Two-line display H1 left (32→72px, tracking 0.008em), aside end-aligned in columns 11–16, then the still bleeds to viewport width (1800/771), then a caption bar with H2 + body + circle-arrow CTA.
FAL-00.good_for: The only hero Falcon currently uses. One still, one CTA, no disclaimer.
FAL-00.source: falconequity.ai (home, approved design — added on Ling's instruction)

FAL-01.anatomy: Featured figure at 80–160px with its label above; two side stats with a 1px ink rule above each value.
FAL-01.good_for: Three confirmed stats from STATS. Never invent one.
FAL-01.source: falconequity.ai (home, approved design — added on Ling's instruction)

FAL-02.anatomy: Eyebrow + H2, then 8 full-width rows on 2px ink rules: title + muted range at columns 1–6, teaser at 8, circle at 12.
FAL-02.good_for: A seven/eight-product menu where each row is a real route.
FAL-02.source: falconequity.ai (home, approved design — added on Ling's instruction)

FAL-03.anatomy: Display quote left at 32–40px, 3:4 still right, 'Falcon client' credit, prev/next circles.
FAL-03.source: falconequity.ai (home, approved design — added on Ling's instruction)

FAL-04.anatomy: Lilac Light field with a select, selected row in Lilac Darker, panel with title + blurbs + circle-arrow + 16:9 still.
FAL-04.source: falconequity.ai (home, approved design — added on Ling's instruction)

FAL-05.shape: Falcon why: dark band, heading left, numbered steps right
FAL-05.anatomy: Darker band. Eyebrow + H2 + body + circle-arrow left; three numbered steps right on 1.5px rules; marquee under.
FAL-05.source: falconequity.ai (home, approved design — added on Ling's instruction)

FAL-06.anatomy: Eyebrow + H2, then three 16:9 cards with titles and a circle-arrow.
FAL-06.source: falconequity.ai (home, approved design — added on Ling's instruction)

OP-00.anatomy: H1 alone at the container's left edge, 56/84 weight 300, display face. No standfirst, no eyebrow, no rule, no breadcrumb, no CTA. 48px top pad, 120px bottom.
OP-00.good_for: Opening a roster, index or lookup page whose answer is the content itself. Do not add a standfirst unless the page has an argument to make.

OP-01.anatomy: H3 claim at 48/72/300 (tracking 0.384px), then a roster grid of 4 tracks x 244px, column gap 96px, row gap 64px (4x244 + 3x96 = 1264, the full container). A fifth item wraps to a second row at the first item's x. Each item is 244x56: name at 18/27/300 over role at 14/21/400, 10px between. No rules, no card chrome, no portraits. Each item is a role=link div with tabindex=0 anchored to #Name-slug.
OP-01.good_for: A leadership, team or advisor list of 3-8 people where the name is the content and no photograph exists. The library's cleanest many-small-units-under-one-claim band.

OP-02.anatomy: An H3 claim at 48/72/300 in the same position as OP-01 with nothing beneath it - the live DOM holds the header block and an empty roster wrapper, so 344px of band carries one line. Its sibling bands render five people each.
OP-02.good_for: Nothing on its own. The spacing (56 above the claim, 160 below) is reusable, but a heading over 160px of white reads as a broken page - populate the roster or cut the band.

OP-03.shape: 4-up name + role roster with bio-length roles
OP-03.anatomy: Identical grid and type to OP-01 (244px tracks, 96/64 gaps, name 18/27/300 over role 14/21/400) but roles are real titles running two to three lines, so the band grows 568 -> 663px while each item keeps its 56px block. Markup carries a has-image class and no portrait ever paints.
OP-03.good_for: The same roster when each role needs a sentence, and the test of whether the grid holds when one role is three lines and its neighbour's is one.

OP-04.shape: search + filter + 5-column record table, load-more and dots
OP-04.anatomy: H4 'Directory' at 32/48/300 in columns 1-8; a 464x66 search field (fill rgb(231,234,238), 1px rgba(0,0,0,.2) border, radius 0, pad 16/24, 32x32 magnifier) with a Filter control at the far right (88x24 + 27x20 sliders SVG). A 1264 table in an overflow-x wrapper: 121px header row, labels 16/24/400, 1px rgb(220,223,229) rule; columns Name 312 / Title 264 / Business Unit 272 / Location 329 / action 87; cells pad 24/40/24/0, rows 76px, copy 18/27.04/300, 1px #dcdfe5 hairline between rows, name cell as th scope=row, Learn More 18/400. Ten rows, then a 240px foot: second Filter left, centred Load More 16/24/300 + 40x40 circle-arrow + 1px divider + dot nav (active 24x24 with a 12px core, others 12x12 at 28px pitch).
OP-04.good_for: Any index of records where each row has one destination. The reusable idea is the desktop table -> mobile accordion swap: at 390 the table collapses to height 0 and an accordion list takes over (74px rows, name + 40px circle-down, opening to 461px with Title/Unit/Location as label-value pairs).
